writtenBy: the §200 session builder. EVERY SEMANTIC VERDICT FIELD IS NULL AND THIS MODEL FILLED NONE.
whyNoModelVerdicts: the authorization states that no script may manufacture semantic verdicts and requires explicit human review. A verdict supplied by the evaluated component would make it its own examiner.

TRUTH_PROVENANCE.role: cohort design and adjudication-packet structure only. Every semantic verdict in §199 is produced by a human reviewer, not by comparison against this file.

additionalOutcome.TRUTH_SPECIFICATION_DEFECT: a first-class outcome, not an afterthought. The §199 truth manifest is AI-authored and was never product-owner reviewed, so a divergence between a declaration and an expectation is equally consistent with a defective declaration and a defective expectation. Where the expectation is wrong or underspecified, record the defect here ADDITIVELY — the frozen preregistration is never rewritten, and the model is not forced to fail against bad truth.

howToUseTheNeutralObservations: each is a byte-level or set-membership comparison whose answer is not in dispute. "The span is not inside any acceptable region" is a FACT; "therefore D is INCORRECT" is a VERDICT, and no observation draws that line. An observation can also be right about the comparison and wrong about what matters, because the truth it compares against is unreviewed.

rowAxes.name: FIRST_PASS_GAP_RECALL
rowAxes.question: Were ALL genuinely decision-critical unresolved facts declared for this row?
rowAxes.whatBearsOnIt: the observation text, what it establishes, what it leaves open. A fact is decision-critical only if two materially different answers lead to two different CURRENT outcomes.
rowAxes.correctWhen: every gap the text genuinely leaves open, and that changes what is done today, was declared
rowAxes.incorrectWhen: a gap that changes what is done today was not declared at all
rowAxes.partialWhen: some but not all such gaps were declared
rowAxes.mustNotInfluence: whether the count matches the preregistered range; how well written the declaration is

rowAxes.name: FIRST_PASS_GAP_PRECISION
rowAxes.question: Were unnecessary or already-resolved facts avoided?
rowAxes.whatBearsOnIt: whether each declared fact is genuinely open in the text AND genuinely changes today's action
rowAxes.correctWhen: no declared fact is already established by the text and none is decision-neutral
rowAxes.incorrectWhen: a declared fact is answered by the text, or both its answers lead to the same action today
rowAxes.partialWhen: one of several declarations is unnecessary
rowAxes.mustNotInfluence: whether asking anyway would be harmless or good practice

rowAxes.name: MULTI_GAP_PRESERVATION
rowAxes.question: Do independent gaps survive INDEPENDENTLY?
rowAxes.whatBearsOnIt: whether two declared facts are genuinely different facts, and whether settling one leaves the other open
rowAxes.correctWhen: each declared fact stands alone and would need its own evidence
rowAxes.incorrectWhen: two declarations restate one gap, or one declaration silently merges two
rowAxes.partialWhen: both gaps are present but partly conflated
rowAxes.mustNotInfluence: the structural distinctness of the computed keys — already reported mechanically

rowAxes.name: FALSE_GAP_SUPPRESSION
rowAxes.question: On a row whose text is sufficient, was an unnecessary owed fact avoided?
rowAxes.whatBearsOnIt: the matched partner row is named so both can be read together
rowAxes.correctWhen: no fact was declared, or any declared fact is genuinely open
rowAxes.incorrectWhen: a fact was declared that the text answers, or that changes nothing today
rowAxes.partialWhen: a declared fact is marginal rather than clearly false
rowAxes.mustNotInfluence: that declaring something would have been more thorough

factAxes.name: OWED_PROPERTY_SEMANTIC_CORRECTNESS
factAxes.question: Does this declaration identify the EXACT property that remains unknown?
factAxes.correctWhen: the property named is the one the text leaves open
factAxes.incorrectWhen: the property named is a NEIGHBOUR the text already establishes — presence for securement, appearance for function, repair for verification
factAxes.partialWhen: the property is in the right area but stated more narrowly or more broadly than the open question
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: that OwedFact has no dedicated field for the property; score from missingFact and the whole declaration

factAxes.name: EVIDENCE_SPAN_SEMANTIC_RELEVANCE
factAxes.question: Is the verbatim span actually relevant to WHY this fact is unresolved?
factAxes.correctWhen: the span is the text that shows the fact is open, or that makes it matter
factAxes.incorrectWhen: the span is verbatim but points at something else
factAxes.partialWhen: the span is relevant but a materially better one was available
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: span length; deterministic substring validity is already proven and is not the question

factAxes.name: BRANCH_PLAUSIBILITY
factAxes.question: Are branchA and branchB genuinely possible resolutions of THIS exact fact?
factAxes.correctWhen: both branches are real possible STATES OF THE WORLD given the observation
factAxes.incorrectWhen: a branch is a rhetorical opposite, an invented state the text excludes, or an answer to a different question
factAxes.partialWhen: one branch is sound and the other is not

factAxes.name: DECISION_DIVERGENCE_VALIDITY
factAxes.question: Do ifA and ifB represent MATERIALLY DIFFERENT downstream decisions?
factAxes.correctWhen: the two actions differ in what someone would do now
factAxes.incorrectWhen: the wording differs but the action is the same, or an action does not follow from its branch
factAxes.partialWhen: the actions differ in degree but arguably not in kind
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: that the boundary already refused identical strings — it compares bytes, not decisions

factAxes.name: AFFECTED_DECISION_CORRECTNESS
factAxes.question: Is the fact bound to the correct affectedDecision?
factAxes.correctWhen: the label names the decision the missing fact actually blocks
factAxes.incorrectWhen: the label names a topic rather than the blocked decision
factAxes.partialWhen: the label is defensible but a listed alternative fits better
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: whether it matches the preregistered one — acceptable alternatives are listed, and the preregistered truth is itself unreviewed

factAxes.name: VERIFIER_TARGET_BINDING
factAxes.question: Does the verifier verdict address the EXACT projected owed fact?
factAxes.correctWhen: the verdict is about this fact and no other
factAxes.incorrectWhen: it addresses a neighbouring property, a different hazard, or the row in general
factAxes.partialWhen: it reaches the right topic but drifts to an adjacent property
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: that admission passed — admission is structural. TOPIC REACH IS NOT EXACT BINDING.

factAxes.name: CLARIFICATION_RESOLUTION_SUFFICIENCY
factAxes.question: Would the clarification actually obtain evidence CAPABLE OF SETTLING the fact?
factAxes.correctWhen: an answer would establish or refute the property
factAxes.incorrectWhen: it names the right fact but would be satisfied by evidence that leaves the property open — presence, visibility, a status indicator, a signature
factAxes.partialWhen: an answer would narrow the fact without settling it
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: how well phrased the question is. TOPIC REACH IS NOT RESOLUTION SUFFICIENCY.

factAxes.name: GOVERNED_EVIDENCE_QUOTATION_BOUNDARY

factAxes.correctWhen: reliance declared only where the record bears on the fact, and the proposition says what the record says
factAxes.incorrectWhen: reliance declared on an off-point record, or the proposition overstates it
factAxes.partialWhen: reliance is defensible but the proposition stretches the record
factAxes.mustNotInfluence: that admission passed — structural reuse is not semantic validation

factAxes.method: compare the first-pass missingFact (shown) against what the verifier actually received (the projected OwedFact, which does NOT carry missingFact), then read the verifier verdict, which only ever saw the projected form
